text:
maya: Hey — running into intermittent 'partial JSON' errors in the Python SSE client when tokens refresh mid-stream. Server sends large JSON objects split across chunks and our parser throws. Anyone seen this pattern?
jon: yep. usually happens when the token refresh triggers a small pause in server-side streaming and chunk boundaries move. Parser needs to reassemble across chunk boundaries.
maya: ok. currently we parse per chunk using json.loads(chunk) and catch ValueError to buffer. feels fragile. is there an existing helper in our SDK?
kevin: Python SDK has a StreamingParser util but it expects NDJSON (
-delimited). Our backend sends single JSON objects that can be split. We could switch to ndjson on the wire, but that'll be a protocol change.
lisa: another angle: add a lightweight reassembly that keeps a bytes buffer and tries incremental decode until it forms a full object. that avoids protocol change.
jon: exactly. incremental approach: append chunk to buffer, try json.loads(buffer.decode()), if fails due to incomplete data, wait for next chunk. only bail for other parse errors.
maya: any gotchas with backpressure? if we keep buffering unbounded we could OOM when a slow consumer lags.
kevin: yeah — implement a max-buffer-bytes and emit an error + reconnect if exceeded. Also pause upstream reads (where supported) so server/transport can backpressure. in asyncio you can call transport.pause_reading().
maya: for sync clients (requests / urllib3) we don't have pause_reading. suggestions?
lisa: for sync, the best you can do is stop iterating and close the connection — that'll tell the server to stop. then reconnect and resume from last event id if the protocol supports it.
jon: also consider sending heartbeat pings from server every 15s to keep connections alive during long processing. if client uses a small read timeout it can avoid spuriously reconnecting.
maya: notes for PR: 1) add incremental JSON reassembler util in python SDK 2) enforce max buffer size + error type 3) docs snippet for handling reconnect + last-event-id 4) mention pause_reading for asyncio clients.
kevin: I'll open the PR for python with tests for split-chunk JSON and buffer-exceeded behavior. assigning to me. :+1:
ci-bot: build queued for branch kevin/sse-reassembler (CI #4578).
maya: for go and js clients — anyone want to check idiomatic pause/read control?
lisa: I'll take JS. suggestion: use a TransformStream that accumulates bytes and emits objects once complete, keep a byteLimit and if exceeded emit an error event.
jon: I'll handle Go — use bufio.Reader with ReadSlice or ReadBytes until a full JSON object can be unmarshaled. track buffer size and return an explicit ErrBufferOverflow.
maya: perfect. thanks everyone. i'll add an RFC note in the SDK repo explaining the recovery path and heartbeat recommendation.
kevin: PR link when ready pls and drop the failing repro snippet here.
maya: will do, repro attached in next message (small script).
